item: Gate 01: without the cheat sheet: navigate anywhere and back; create, move, and delete a file; recall a command with CtrlR; start, split, detach, and reattach tmux; a commit in your log for every day so far.
Gate 02: find any file by name and any string by content in a repo you've never seen; jump between three projects with z; resurrect yesterday's commands without retyping them.
Gate 03: cold start to full workspace in one command; move between editor, terminal, and browser without touching the mouse; survive a detach in the middle of real work.
Gate 04: stage half a file with add -p; explain what HEAD is in one sentence; undo an unstaged change, a staged change, and a bad commit; branch and merge without consulting anything.
Gate 05: make five common edits without arrow keys or mouse; open any file by fuzzy name; move between editor and terminal panes without thinking about it.
Gate 06: compose a pipeline from scratch to answer a question; write, run, and lint a script; push a branch and open a PR without looking anything up.
Gate 07: write a loop, a dict lookup, and a function from a blank file; make a failing test pass; read a traceback bottom-up and say what it means before fixing it.
Gate 08: create a table and query it with WHERE/GROUP BY from memory; run the SELECT-before-UPDATE ritual unprompted; explain tables-vs-documents in two sentences using your own data as the example.

Gate 09: explain request/response and a status code in plain words; fetch, store, and serve the same piece of data; find your way around a codebase you've never seen well enough to describe one file's job.
Gate 10: run the full loop without skipping review; produce a red test an agent can work from; notice a polluted context before it costs you an hour.
Gate 11: a fresh agent session follows your AGENTS.md without coaching; you catch a plan-reality divergence before merge; the SELECT-before-write and risk-naming habits fire without prompting.
